items.title: Fred Lipsius interviewed by Monk Rowe. Boston, Massachusetts, July 25, 2018
items.q: It reminds me there’s an anecdote about Bix Beiderbecke when he was living, near the end of his life

ctx.x: Yeah, when we moved to another place. Because someone had complained. They got a complaint, I used to go to school with him, his son played clarinet better than me and influenced me a little bit. But he called me up one day, I’m like, you know, public school. You know, I don’t want to go into it. He said — my parents weren’t on the phone it was just me. And he says, “You know you’re not supposed to play more than an hour.” And it put the fear into me. So I had years of being afraid of playing. Even now I mean I…

It reminds me there’s an anecdote about Bix Beiderbecke when he was living, near the end of his life, and he was playing in this house where he was staying and he thought he was bothering people and they go, “No, no, keep playing.”
